critical_code_review_comments: server.py _seed_second_clinic() password-resync loop at lines 312-319 only updates the password_hash when the existing password fails verify — but it never also re-sets clinic_id if the user was previously assigned to a different clinic. If someone manually moved a Delhi user to Mumbai, restart would not pull them back. Low-risk (demo-only), but Mumbai seed at lines 259-267 has the same pattern, so consistent behaviour.

routers/reports.py share-link 401 'Share link clinic mismatch' is correct, but the log-line does not include the attacker-supplied clinic_id vs. session.clinic_id for forensic use. Adding it to the audit-log would help HIPAA-style access review.

billing.py DI convergence is clean — every endpoint is now db=Depends(get_db). No remaining references to _db() or attach_db(). Grep verified: `grep -n '_db()\|attach_db' /app/backend/billing.py` returns empty.

ReportHandoverPage.shareWhatsAppWithPdf() line 67 probes the PDF blob via axios even on desktop, then uses canShare to decide — this means every desktop click still downloads ~50-100KB of PDF bytes to memory before falling through. For large PDFs on slow connections this is wasted bandwidth. Consider skipping the blob probe when !navigator.canShare at the top of the function.

ReportHandoverPage line 93-106 last-ditch fallback still triggers a download when share-link mint fails — this is the OLD behaviour. It's defensive but worth documenting in a code comment so future devs don't think it's the main path.

Test-authoring drift this iteration (fixed locally, NOT product bugs): billing invoice/service create payloads use 'lines' (not 'items') and 'price' (not 'base_price'); /api/patient-notes requires patient_id query param (not listable without it). Noted for context_for_next_testing_agent.
